messages:
sam: Heads up — after the v2.0.0 tag, our customers' builds fail with module path error. Example error:

sam: ```
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.0: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood/inference-go
	but was required as: github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
```

maria: can you paste your go.mod and the import you're using?

sam: go.mod in consumer app shows:
```
module github.com/customer/app

require (
	github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 v2.0.0
)
```
imports: `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2` — so consumer is correct

alex: looks like upstream tag v2.0.0 has a go.mod without /v2 in module path. That breaks semver for v2+. Release must have updated module path to include `/v2` when tagging.

jen: Confirmed — release pushed tag v2.0.0 but forgot to update module path. Working on a fix. short-term workaround: run `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v1.9.2` or add a replace in your go.mod:
```
replace github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 => github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.0.0
```
But prefer: use `go get github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2@v2.0.1` once we publish corrected tag.

sam: replace workaround fixed local build for me, thx.

jen: We've opened PR to update module path and will cut v2.0.1 with correct go.mod. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-go/pull/498 — ETA 2h. I'll ping @eng-release.

release-bot: deploy created for tag v2.0.1 (draft) — ci/verify failing due to go proxy cache, will force update.

alex: long-term: add CI check that fails release if major tag doesn't match module path (v2 tag requires /v2 in module). I'll make a ticket.

maria: customers affected?
sam: two customers reported build errors this morning, one internal CI. escalated to priority-1.

jen: adding to status, will also post a short note to changelog and support templates. :thumbsup:

sam: great, appreciate the quick turnaround.
